outcomes: Center a two-feature dataset and compute sample covariance
Find a leading eigenvector with checked power iteration
Fit PCA state, transform rows into projection scores, and reconstruct them
Interpret explained variance, eigengaps, and covariance conditioning
lessons: Turn correlated columns into a matrix
Find the direction by repeated multiplication
Conditioning tells you when answers wobble

pca.name: principal component analysis
pca.definition: A linear method that represents centered data along orthogonal directions of decreasing variance.
pca.explanation: PCA finds covariance eigenvectors and orders them by eigenvalue. Fitting estimates and stores the mean, covariance, components, and eigenvalues from training rows. Transforming later rows uses that stored state without refitting. Keeping the first k directions compresses each d-feature row into k projection scores, and multiplying those scores by the directions reconstructs an approximation. PCA is unsupervised: it preserves variation, which need not be useful for prediction. Discarded directions cannot be recovered from the compressed scores.

covariance.name: covariance
covariance.definition: A measure of how two centered features vary together across rows.
covariance.explanation: The covariance matrix stores feature variances on its diagonal and pairwise covariances off the diagonal. This chapter uses sample covariance with denominator n-1. Positive covariance means two features tend to be above or below their means together; negative covariance means they tend to move oppositely. Covariance depends on units, so raw and standardized PCA can produce very different components. Its matrix is symmetric by construction.

eigenvector.name: eigenvector
eigenvector.definition: A nonzero direction that a matrix scales without rotating, satisfying Cq = lambda q.
eigenvector.explanation: For a covariance matrix, an eigenvector is a direction through feature space and its eigenvalue is the sample variance along that direction. PCA keeps eigenvectors with the largest eigenvalues. The sign is arbitrary because q and -q span the same axis. When eigenvalues are nearly tied, individual eigenvectors may rotate under tiny perturbations even when their combined subspace remains useful.

projection.name: projection
projection.definition: The dot-product coordinate of a centered row along a unit component direction.
projection.explanation: For component q and stored mean mu, the projection score is q transpose times x minus mu. It is a geometric coordinate, distinct from a classifier score that measures evidence before a class decision. A one-component reconstruction adds the mean to q times that projection score. Forgetting to center forces the approximation through the origin and breaks translation invariance. Projection reduces dimension, but discarded orthogonal directions cannot be recovered from the retained coordinate.

power-iteration.name: power iteration
power-iteration.definition: Repeated matrix multiplication and normalization used to estimate a dominant eigenvector.
power-iteration.explanation: Each iteration multiplies a direction by the matrix, then divides by its Euclidean norm. When the largest eigenvalue magnitude is unique and the start overlaps its eigenvector, the dominant contribution grows relative to others. A start exactly orthogonal to that direction fails, so the two-dimensional reference tries two independent starts. Unit norm and a small eigenpair residual provide direct correctness checks.

condition-number.name: condition number
condition-number.definition: For positive covariance, the ratio of largest to smallest eigenvalue.
condition-number.explanation: A large covariance condition number indicates a nearly flat direction. This can signal strong compressibility, but any later division by the small eigenvalue amplifies noise. Forming covariance as centered-data transpose times centered-data squares the original matrix condition number. Production PCA therefore often uses singular-value decomposition rather than explicitly forming covariance, especially for high-dimensional or ill-conditioned data. Infinite condition number indicates an exactly zero-variance direction.

checks: Power iteration recovers eigenvalue 3 for the matrix [[2,1],[1,2]]
The returned component has unit norm and a small eigenpair residual
Translating all rows preserves eigenvalues, directions, and reconstruction error
Rank-one data reconstructs with negligible one-component error
Mean squared reconstruction norm divides summed squared row norms by the number of rows
Too few or nonfinite rows are rejected
limitations: The reference supports two features and one retained component
Two fixed independent starts are not a general eigensolver
Explicit covariance can lose accuracy on badly conditioned data
The reported reconstruction statistic averages squared Euclidean norms per row rather than squared residuals per coordinate
The Wine extension requires a user-prepared attributed dataset
